prose_updates.tldr: SparseSIM-ID starts from finite state spaces, an exact conditional-independence oracle, background orientations, and a causal query; a rational realization and a compressed graph family are optional checked accelerators. It certifies oracle realizability, exhaustively constructs every minimum-edge DAG I-map, and uses exact pairwise positive-chamber decisions to compute the unique coarsest quotient whose classes share \(P_x(Y)\) on the strictly positive exact-oracle model. Each pairwise decision returns either a finite universal-equality certificate or an exact real-algebraic positive ambiguity table. Normalization reduces the all-pairs feasibility count to \(\binom{|\mathfrak D|}{2}(\prod_{v\in Y}|\Omega_v|-1)\), and the reference-only common-effect test to \((|\mathfrak D|-1)(\prod_{v\in Y}|\Omega_v|-1)\). For every fixed or externally certified true quotient class \(C\), the representative circuit supports a multivariate plug-in central limit theorem, consistent sandwich covariance, and Wald intervals for fixed contrasts; this is not inference after data-driven oracle or class selection. The explicit four-binary-variable rational cross-MEC witness remains a strictness certificate.

project_justification.gap: Existing simultaneous-identification criteria are sufficient graphical tests and do not compute the maximal law-restricted effect quotient across all tied minimum-edge DAG I-maps. Saturated conditional-independence ideals also do not select strict positivity or the bit-zero exact-oracle chamber, and a one-class inferential formulation omits valid class-specific targets when several effect classes are returned.
project_justification.niche: For finite observed variables, the exact oracle, every admissible DAG, every graphwise truncated functional, and every arbitrary-pair positive-chamber equality test are finite and exact. This makes the tied-sparsest family and its maximal causal-effect quotient computable, while a fixed representative circuit in any returned class is an ordinary smooth rational functional at a strictly positive law.
project_justification.fill: The project gives a terminating realizability-first algorithm that enumerates all minimum-edge I-map ties, partitions them through exact pairwise semialgebraic decisions, and certifies every merge or separation. It returns one observable circuit per class and algebraic-number ambiguity witnesses across classes. Conditional on fixing or externally certifying the true quotient class, it also supplies class-specific plug-in Gaussian inference, a consistent sandwich covariance, and Wald intervals for arbitrary fixed nondegenerate contrasts.

prose_updates.related_work: Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo (2025, Theorem 3.2 and Section 4.2) give the closest simultaneous-identification boundary: their SA-MPDAG condition is sufficient, whereas SparseSIM-ID decides and certifies the complete effect quotient of every finite tied minimum-edge I-map family. The preserved four-node rational example lies outside that graphical sufficient region and has two distinct causal values. Perkovic (2020, Theorem 3.6) supplies single-MPDAG identification structure, but no extensional equivalence with the present law-restricted cross-family quotient is claimed. Guo and Perkovic (2021, Theorem 3) minimally enumerate graph-generic effect functionals within one MPDAG; the proved relation is one-way: a class they certify as one functional is contained in a SparseSIM-ID class whenever the exact-oracle model is contained in that MPDAG's positive Markov model. Garcia, Stillman, and Sturmfels (2005) inform saturation, while Tarski's decision method and Stengle's Positivstellensatz provide supporting exact feasibility machinery rather than the causal novelty. Kahle, Rauh, and Sullivant (2017) explain why irrelevant conditional-independence components preclude reading positive exact-oracle separation from ideal nonmembership. Raskutti and Uhler (2018) motivate retention of all sparsest ties; the new output policy quotients those ties by the causal query. Chang, Guo, and Malinsky (2024) provide post-PC selection-aware interval unions, whereas the present plug-in theorem is pointwise for a fixed or externally certified true quotient class and explicitly makes no claim after data-driven class or oracle selection. Jaber, Zhang, and Bareinboim (2019) and Duarte et al. (2024) remain adjacent completeness and optimization comparators rather than equivalent results.

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from one fixed strictly positive multinomial law \(P\), conditional on a real-realizable exact oracle, its tied minimum-edge family, and one true returned quotient class \(C\) having been fixed in advance or certified externally; the class is not selected from the same sample used for inference.
sampling_model.overlap: Membership \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) gives positive cells and therefore positive recorded marginal denominators for every representative circuit at the fixed law.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no nonparametric nuisances. For the canonical representative \(R_C\), compute \(\widehat\tau_{C,n}=\tau_C(\widehat p_n)\), \(\widehat\Sigma_n=\operatorname{diag}(\widehat p_n)-\widehat p_n\widehat p_n^{\mathsf T}\), and \(\widehat V_{C,n}=J_{\tau_C}(\widehat p_n)\widehat\Sigma_nJ_{\tau_C}(\widehat p_n)^{\mathsf T}\) on the positive-denominator event.

prose_updates.honest_scope: The required inputs are finite state spaces, a complete exact conditional-independence bit-vector, background orientations, and a causal query. A rational realization and a compressed SA-MPDAG or CPDAG family are optional checked accelerators, not assumptions. Unrealizable exact oracles and background systems admitting no I-map receive finite rejection certificates; every real-realizable oracle with at least one admissible DAG proceeds to the complete tied minimum-edge quotient. Each arbitrary-pair decision returns either exact universal-equality evidence or an exact real-algebraic positive separator. Separators need not be rational, and no polynomial-time or uniform height guarantee is made. The quotient is law-restricted and can be coarser than a graph-generic within-MPDAG enumeration; only the proved one-way Guo--Perkovic containment is claimed. The four-variable table remains an explicit rational cross-MEC separator with values \(13/20\) and \(1/2\). Plug-in inference applies to every fixed or externally certified true quotient class and to fixed nondegenerate contrasts, but it is pointwise and is not selection-aware inference for an oracle, graph family, or class estimated from the same data.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Termination and the numbers of pairwise positive-chamber comparisons are explicit, but no favorable running-time, degree, certificate-length, or algebraic-height bound is claimed. The default DAG enumeration is finite and may be exponential or worse. Saturation by cells and denominators excludes components contained in their zero sets but imposes neither positivity nor bit-zero nonvanishing, so a nonzero normal form is only a feasibility trigger. General feasible separators are guaranteed to be exact real algebraic, not rational. The rational-replacement question remains open only for an already feasible set \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\{F_{D,D',y}\neq0\}\) and is not needed for pairwise decision or quotient completeness. The plug-in central limit theorem is conditional on a fixed or externally certified true quotient class; uniformity and post-selection coverage after estimating the oracle or class are not established.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem is the exact pairwise kernel of the maximal quotient: for any two tied DAGs and any outcome cell, it produces independently checkable evidence for either universal equality or positive-chamber separation.
statement_notes.gap: Ideal nonmembership can be witnessed on an irrelevant component or sign chamber, so neither saturation nor a nonzero normal form decides separation on the strictly positive exact-oracle model.
statement_notes.consumer: The quotient algorithm can merge arbitrary graph pairs only with equality certificates and split them only with an exact real-algebraic table at which their intervention laws differ.

statement_notes.justification: Every fixed returned quotient class has one representative smooth rational circuit, so it supports one multivariate plug-in limit law, one consistent sandwich covariance, and Wald inference for fixed contrasts.
statement_notes.gap: This pointwise theorem conditions on a fixed or externally certified true quotient class and does not replace selection-aware procedures when the oracle or class is estimated from the same data.
statement_notes.consumer: After population discovery or external certification, practitioners can estimate any class-specific intervention vector and form exact-quantile Wald intervals for nondegenerate fixed contrasts.
